⚡The energy transition is about Jobs. But where and for who ?
 
Renewable energy employment reached a record 16.6 million jobs globally in 2024.
 
Yet more than 85% of those jobs are concentrated in just five countries and regions.
 
That raises a bigger question: the energy transition is creating enormous economic value — but who will have the opportunity to create, own and benefit from it?
 
A just transition is not only about creating more green jobs.
 
🏭 It is about socio-economic development, where new industries and supply chains are built. Between 2018 and 2024, China accounted for around 80% of global investment in manufacturing facilities for solar, wind, batteries and hydrogen technologies.
 
💰 It is about where investment flows. Low- and lower-middle-income countries are home to more than 40% of the world’s population, yet account for only 7% of global clean energy spending. In emerging and developing economies, the cost of capital for renewable energy projects can be two to three times higher than in advanced economies.
 
👷 It is about whether workers can access the opportunities being created. Around 60% of energy companies report labour shortages, and the number of graduates entering the energy sector would need to increase by around 40% by 2030 just to prevent today’s skills mismatch from worsening.
 
⚡ And it is about whether the transition ultimately delivers for people and planet. Even as clean energy investment and employment reach record levels, 655 million people worldwide still live without electricity.
 
These numbers are connected.
 
Where investment and manufacturing concentrate, jobs and economic value tend to follow.
 
For developing economies, a just transition must therefore be about more than replacing one energy source with another. It must help create decent jobs, build local industries and skills, expand affordable and reliable energy access, mobilize investment and support economic diversification.
 
As #UNGA81 gathers momentum, the question is not only how fast we can move. It is how we ensure more countries, communities and people can participate in creating the value generated by the transition — and share in its benefits.
 
Speed matters. But so does where the transition takes us — and who gets there with us.

#JustEnergyTransition #EnergyForDevelopment #SDG7
